newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Ford manager sounds warning to unions.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Ford manager sounds warning to unions.

text.p: Peter Heller, director of Ford Motor Co's Belgian production unit, on Monday warned that strike action in sympathy with Renault Belgium workers could tempt other car makers to pull out of Belgium.
"When I hear that unions want to stage a national strike at other car manufacturers, they are big idiots...They attract the attention of all those constructors to Belgium," Heller told Reuters.

"Some of those multinationals may begin to believe that what Renault is doing is perhaps not that bad. (They may think) in Belgium you can close a factory without losing a lot of market share because it is just a small market," he said.
French car maker Renault announced last Thursday it would close its assembly plant in Vilvoorde near Brussels as part of a reorganisation of production.
About 3,100 jobs will be lost at Renault Belgium and another 1,000 at suppliers and subcontractors.

Unions are up in arms over Renault's decision and are expected to propose for Friday a 24-hour strike in the car sector in Belgium, where several constructors -- Ford, Opel, Volvo, Renault and Volkswagen -- have large assembly plants.
About 400 workers in the body parts division of Volkswagen's Brussels assembly plant held a two-hour stoppage earlier on Monday, a union spokesman told the Belga news agency.
He said personnel at the plant, a wholly-owned unit of German car maker Volkswagen AG, went back to work only after unions promised to propose the 24-hour strike.
The VW plant has a total workforce of nearly 6,000 and assembles about 200,000 Golf and Passat cars per year.
VW was not immediately available for comment.
A decision on the strike will not be taken until after auto workers union representatives meet at Renault Belgium on Tuesday.

Heller was commenting more widely on the Belgian motor industry after denying a weekend report that Ford might move its Transit van production to Britain from Belgium. Ford's plant in Genk, north eastern Belgium, has a workforce of 12,000, making it Belgium's largest automotive plant.
